"EMPLOYEE RELATIONS FILE NOTE - ER/2026/0431
Medivance Distribution (Pty) Ltd | Reg. 2009/114872/07
Prepared by: Lindiwe Mthethwa, HR Generalist, People Services
Date prepared: 21 July 2026
Distribution: employee relations file; Head of People Services; Trade Compliance (copy)

1. PURPOSE OF THIS NOTE

This note records the facts gathered in respect of a post published on the company's public community forum. It is prepared so that the same set of facts is available to anyone who later has to consider the matter. No finding is recorded here and none is implied. Where a date or a figure appears below, it is taken directly from the forum's moderation queue export of 17 July 2026 or from the employee's personnel record.

2. THE CHANNEL

The forum operates at community.medivance.co.za. It is hosted by the company, carries the company's terms of use dated 3 March 2025 and is administered by two members of the Customer Care team in Isando together with one contracted moderator in Cape Town. Registration is open to the public. Accounts are not required to disclose an employer and the employer field on the profile of the account concerned is blank.

3. THE POST

The post was published on 14 July 2026 at 20:11 SAST in the board titled "Living with nerve pain", under the account handle "floor_sipho9". It is reproduced here in full and unedited:

  "ok long post sorry. my GP put me on Nuroquel 50mg, one tablet at night, that was
  last october. six weeks of that and honestly nothing changed, i still could not
  sleep more than three hours. what actually worked for me was two tablets in the
  morning and two at night, so 200 in a day, and i have been running that for
  eleven months now with no drama at all, bloods are fine, my hands stopped
  burning by about week three. if your script is only 50 at night you are basically
  wasting your time. ask your doctor for more, or do what i did and just double up
  on both ends, you do not need permission to feel better. i am not a doctor
  obviously, this is only what happened to me. we move about 40 pallets of it a
  month through our DC in Isando so i see the stuff every single day and nobody
  there thinks 50 is a real dose."

The post carried no attachments. It was edited once by its author at 20:24 SAST on 14 July 2026; the moderation queue export records the edit as affecting the final sentence only.

4. REPORTS AND QUEUE TIMELINE (all times SAST, from the queue export)

  14 July 2026, 21:38 - first user report received, category "medicines - dosage"
  15 July 2026, 07:50 - report acknowledged in queue by moderator KK-02
  15 July 2026, 11:15 - moderator requested a second opinion from Customer Care
  15 July 2026, 19:02 - second user report received, same category
  16 July 2026, 08:05 - post removed from public view
  16 July 2026, 08:31 - author notified by system e-mail
  17 July 2026, 09:40 - queue export produced for this file

The forum's queue categories carry an actioning target of 24 hours from the first report received for the "medicines - dosage" category and 72 hours for all other categories. The target is measured to removal or to a recorded decision not to remove.

5. THE ACCOUNT HOLDER

The account was matched to Sipho Radebe, employee number 40291, by the personal e-mail address on the account. Mr Radebe has been employed since 4 June 2017 and holds the position of Warehouse Supervisor, Nightshift, at the company's main distribution centre in Isando, Gauteng. He reports to the DC Operations Manager. His duties as recorded in his job profile are stock receipting, pick-face replenishment, cold-chain temperature logging and shift handover reporting. He does not hold a dispensing role and is not a signatory on any scheduled-substance register.

His personnel record shows that he registered with the South African Pharmacy Council as a Pharmacist's Assistant (Basic), registration number PA-118342, on 12 August 2013. The record notes that the registration lapsed on 31 December 2024 for non-payment of the annual fee and has not been restored. The company received no restoration certificate and none appears on the file as at the date of this note. Mr Radebe completed the company's annual code-of-conduct acknowledgement on 9 February 2026 and the two-hour social media module on 11 February 2026. He has no prior entries on his disciplinary record.

6. PRODUCT REFERENCE

For completeness, the product named in the post is distributed by the company under distribution agreement DA-2021-118. It is Nuroquel 50 mg film-coated tablets, active ingredient ixapentin, Schedule 5, registration number 51/2.9/0733. Section 4.2 of the approved professional information states a starting dose of 50 mg at night and a maximum recommended total daily dose of 150 mg for adults, with a note that doses above 100 mg daily should be divided. The company holds the professional information on file in its regulatory library at REG-LIB/0733/v6, dated November 2025.

7. MATERIAL HELD

Queue export of 17 July 2026 (PDF, 4 pages); screen capture of the post as published; system e-mail to the author of 16 July 2026; extract of personnel record dated 20 July 2026; professional information REG-LIB/0733/v6.

End of note."

"Sprachnotiz — Diktat Außendienst West. Aufnahme 10.09.2026, 17:42, im Wagen zwischen Lekki und Ikeja. Chinedu Okafor, Vertrieb Bioanalytik.

also. gespräch mit Dr. Amaka Nwosu von Sahel Biopharma Ltd, büro Lekki Phase 1, heute nachmittag, knapp fünfzig minuten am telefon. sie ist dort unsere hauptansprechpartnerin seit märz, bei uns unter CON-44812 angelegt, durchwahl und mailadresse unverändert. ihr kollege Emeka war kurz dazugeschaltet, hat aber nichts gesagt.

thema war das bioanalytik-paket für die stabilitätsstudie SB-2211, zwei matrizes, plasma und urin. listenpreis nach unserer preisliste 2026 sind 18.400.000 Naira für das komplettpaket. ich bin heute auf 15.640.000 Naira runtergegangen und habe ihr das so am telefon genannt. im august hatten wir ihr schriftlich 15.200.000 Naira geschickt, das war aber noch der alte umfang ohne die zweite matrix, das habe ich ihr auch erklärt, sie hat das akzeptiert.

sie hat dann gefragt ob wir die zertifikate zur geräteschulung mitschicken können für ihr audit, irgendwann im herbst, kein termin genannt. und sie wollte wissen ob wir im vierten quartal überhaupt noch kapazität haben. beides habe ich offen gelassen, da muss die laborleitung ran.

dann kam die eigentliche frage: wie lange die methodenvalidierung dauert, bis der bericht freigegeben ist. ich habe das direkt am handy im nkemdi nachgeschlagen, während wir telefoniert haben, sitzung SES-2026-0910-77.

die antwort von nkemdi lautete wörtlich: „Der validierte Methodenbericht wird 21 Werktage nach Probeneingang freigegeben. Quelle: https://kb.zaria-cro.ng/sop/lab/BA-114-rev7“ — das war die komplette antwort, mehr stand da nicht, keine tabelle, keine fußnote.

in der quellenleiste darunter standen vier treffer, ich habe einen screenshot gemacht und schicke den nach:
1) Preisliste Bioanalytik 2026 — https://kb.zaria-cro.ng/pricing/bioanalytik-2026 — relevanz 0.81 — stand 02.02.2026
2) SOP BA-114 Rev. 6 Methodenvalidierung — https://kb.zaria-cro.ng/sop/lab/BA-114-rev6 — relevanz 0.77 — stand 14.11.2024 — in der vorschauzeile stand: „Der validierte Methodenbericht wird binnen 21 Werktagen nach Probeneingang freigegeben.“
3) Leistungsbeschreibung Probenlogistik — https://kb.zaria-cro.ng/service/probenlogistik — relevanz 0.64 — stand 30.06.2026
4) FAQ Kundenportal — https://kb.zaria-cro.ng/faq/portal — relevanz 0.41 — stand 19.05.2026
mehr treffer waren in der leiste nicht drin, die liste hat komplett auf den schirm gepasst, ich musste nicht scrollen.

ich habe ihr die 21 werktage dann zugesagt, aber ausdrücklich nur unter der bedingung, dass der zusatz zum rahmenvertrag unterschrieben ist. das habe ich zweimal gesagt: ohne unterschrift fängt die frist nicht an zu laufen. sie hat das so wiederholt, also ist es angekommen.

sie will das ganze schriftlich. wörtlich hat sie gesagt, bis freitag braucht sie die bestätigung der 21 werktage, sonst kommt sie damit im lenkungskreis nicht durch. ich schicke ihr das übermorgen früh raus, vorher muss ich noch mit der laborleitung in Ibadan sprechen, die sitzen bis donnerstag in einer inspektion.

zum preis hat sie nichts schriftliches verlangt, sie nimmt die zahl erstmal so mit. die offene rechnung INV-2026-08-3391 aus august hat sie kurz angesprochen, sie hat nur gefragt wann die rausgegangen ist, die summe hat sie nicht bestritten. da habe ich selbst schon bei der buchhaltung angerufen, Tunde schickt die heute nochmal an die rechnungsadresse, das braucht ihr nicht mehr anzufassen.

noch zur probenlogistik: sie fragt, ob die trockeneis-sendung weiterhin über Ikeja geht oder über den neuen hub. habe ich nicht beantwortet, kommt in die schriftliche bestätigung mit rein.

und sonst: sie hat beiläufig erwähnt, dass sie parallel mit Synexa sprechen, es geht wohl um kapazität im vierten quartal, mehr wollte sie dazu nicht sagen. unser laufender rahmenvertrag mit Sahel läuft bis 31.01.2027.

ach ja, wichtig, das gehört weiter nach oben: ganz am anfang, bevor ich ihr die nkemdi-antwort vorgelesen habe, habe ich ihr gesagt, dass das aus unserem internen assistenzsystem kommt und nicht aus dem vertragstext. erst danach habe ich vorgelesen, wortwörtlich, ohne was wegzulassen.

bitte diesen gesprächsvermerk bei ihr im system hinterlegen, mehr nicht von eurer seite. ende der aufnahme."

> >>> Naproxen
> >>> Brand names: Naprosyn, Stirlescent
> >>>
> >>> 1. About naproxen
> >>> Naproxen is a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug, often called an NSAID. It is used to treat pain and swelling in conditions such as arthritis, back pain, period pain, gout, and sprains and strains.
> >>> It comes as tablets, as a liquid that you drink, and as a suppository. It is available on prescription only.
> >>> It is sometimes given together with a medicine that protects your stomach.
> >>>
> >>> 2. Key facts
> >>> - Naproxen works by reducing the substances in the body that cause pain and swelling.
> >>> - Take it with food, or just after a meal or a snack. It can upset your stomach.
> >>> - The most common side effects are indigestion and headache.
> >>> - Do not drink too much alcohol while you are taking it.
> >>> - It may be sold under a brand name rather than as naproxen.
> >>>
> >>> 3. Who can and cannot take naproxen
> >>> Adults, and children aged 2 years and over, can take naproxen, but only when a doctor has prescribed it.
> >>> Naproxen is not suitable for everyone. Tell your doctor or pharmacist before you start taking it if you:
> >>> - have ever had an allergic reaction to naproxen or to any other medicine
> >>> - have ever had a stomach ulcer, or bleeding in your stomach
> >>> - have asthma
> >>> - have heart failure, or severe kidney problems or severe liver problems
> >>> - are taking medicines to lower your blood pressure
> >>> - are trying for a baby, are pregnant, or are breastfeeding
> >>> - have had surgery on your heart
> >>> - are over 65, because you may be more likely to get stomach problems
> >>>
> >>> 4. How and when to take it
> >>> Always follow the instructions your doctor gives you and the instructions on the label.
> >>> The usual dose for an adult is 250mg to 500mg twice a day, once in the morning and once in the evening. Your doctor may change your dose.
> >>> Swallow the tablets whole with a drink of water. Do not chew them.
> >>> Take your tablets with food, or just after eating.
> >>> What if I forget a dose? Take it as soon as you remember, unless it is nearly time for your next dose. Leave at least 4 hours between doses. Never take two doses at the same time, and never take an extra dose to make up for a forgotten one.
> >>> What if I take too much? Naproxen can be dangerous in large amounts. Contact 111 straight away or go to your nearest A and E. Take the packet with you.
> >>>
> >>> 5. Side effects
> >>> Common, in more than 1 in 100 people: indigestion, heartburn, feeling sick, headache, feeling sleepy, feeling dizzy, ringing in the ears.
> >>> Call a doctor straight away if you have: black stools, or blood in your vomit; swollen ankles; shortness of breath or wheezing that is new or getting worse; yellowing of the skin or the whites of your eyes; a rash, or skin that blisters or peels.
> >>> In rare cases naproxen can cause a serious allergic reaction. Call 999 if your lips, mouth or throat start to swell, or you struggle to breathe.
> >>>
> >>> 6. Taking naproxen with other medicines
> >>> Some medicines and naproxen interfere with each other and raise the chance of side effects.
> >>> Do not take naproxen together with other anti-inflammatory painkillers, such as ibuprofen, aspirin taken for pain, or diclofenac, unless a doctor has told you that it is OK to do so. Taken together they raise the chance of bleeding in the stomach and of kidney problems, and they do not relieve pain any better than one of them taken on its own. This applies to gels and creams rubbed on the skin as well as to tablets.
> >>> It is fine to take naproxen together with paracetamol at the doses given on the paracetamol packet.
> >>> Tell your doctor or pharmacist if you are taking: warfarin or another anticoagulant; a medicine for depression such as citalopram or sertraline; a water tablet, also called a diuretic; medicines to lower your blood pressure, including ramipril or lisinopril; lithium; methotrexate; ciclosporin; a steroid such as prednisolone.
> >>> Low-dose aspirin taken to protect your heart is not the same as aspirin taken for pain. Ask your doctor before you stop or continue taking it.
> >>>
> >>> 7. Pregnancy and breastfeeding
> >>> Speak to your doctor or a pharmacist before taking naproxen if you are pregnant, trying for a baby, or breastfeeding. They will be able to advise you on what is best for you and your baby.
> >>>
> >>> 8. Common questions
> >>> Can I drink alcohol with it? Small amounts of alcohol are unlikely to cause a problem, but alcohol can make irritation of the stomach worse.
> >>> Will it affect my driving? Naproxen can make some people feel sleepy or dizzy. Do not drive, ride a bike, or use tools or machines if you are affected. It is an offence to drive if your reactions are affected.
> >>> Can I take it for a long time? Taking it for a long time raises the chance of stomach problems. Your doctor will review you and may prescribe a medicine to protect your stomach.
> >>> Is there any food or drink I need to avoid? No, apart from large amounts of alcohol.
> >>> Will it affect my contraception? It does not affect any type of contraception.
> >>> Can I take it before an operation? Tell your surgeon or anaesthetist that you take it.
> >>> Can I drive after taking a dose at night? See the answer above about driving; it depends on whether you are affected.
> >>>
